name: AMD Pitcairn PRO (Radeon R9 M380 / M390 class, GCN 1.0 / Southern Islands)

linux.summary: amdgpu binds automatically on modern kernels; Display Core initialises on DCE 6.0. Reports Display Core v3.2.369, 2048 MB GDDR5, 256-bit. Connectors exposed: eDP-1, DP-1, DP-2, DP-3.

caveats.detail: amdgpu logs 'Skipping amdgpu DM backlight registration' on DCE 6.0. Brightness cannot be adjusted from software.

caveats.summary: Native 5120x2880 does not work; the internal panel is limited to 3840x2160.
caveats.detail: 5120x2880@60 needs two DisplayPort channels. DCE 6.0 is DisplayPort 1.2, so a link caps at HBR2 (4 lanes x 5.4 Gbps = 21.6 Gbps raw, ~17.28 Gbps payload after 8b/10b, ~720 MHz pixel clock at 24bpp); reduced-blanking 5K60 needs ~938 MHz and does not fit. One channel suffices for 3840x2160@60. The EDID has a CTA-861 extension but no DisplayID tile block, so the 5K mode is never advertised (not kernel mode pruning). Forcing video=eDP-1:5120x2880@60 yields 'User-defined mode not supported'. Widely circulated forum advice (amdgpu.dc=1 amdgpu.mst=1 video=eDP-1:5120x2880@60) comes from 2017/2019 Polaris iMacs with DisplayPort 1.4 / HBR3 where 5K60 fits on one link, and does not apply to this DCE 6.0 machine.

workarounds.problem: No DRM driver binds; only simpledrm with a card0-Unknown-1 connector, no external outputs, no hotplug.
workarounds.cause: nomodeset on the kernel command line, commonly added to get the installer running.
workarounds.fix: Remove nomodeset from GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT, then run update-grub and reboot. Diagnostic signature: 'lspci -nnk' shows no 'Kernel driver in use:' line for the VGA device.

workarounds.problem: Older kernels bind the legacy radeon driver instead of amdgpu.
workarounds.fix: Force Southern Islands to amdgpu via kernel parameters.
